[p. 406]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah An-Naba' (The Great News)

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿About what do they question one another?﴾ ﴿About the great news﴾ ﴿concerning which they are in disagreement.﴾ ﴿No! They will soon know.﴾ ﴿Again, no! They will soon know.﴾

﴿'Amma﴾ originally was ʿan mā, and the nūn was assimilated into the mīm (idghām, the merging of one consonant into another). Then the alif of mā was deleted because the preposition had entered upon it, to distinguish the interrogative mā from the relative mā.

The meaning is: "About what thing do they question one another?" The preposition may be separated from mā, in which case the alif is not deleted.

Al-Zamakhsharī cited the verse of Ḥassān (may Allah be pleased with him):

*"Because of what a base man stood up to revile me, like a pig that rolls in ashes."*

In al-Kashshāf, al-Zamakhsharī said: It is narrated from Ibn Kathīr that he recited ﴿ʿammah﴾ with the silent hāʾ (hāʾ al-sakt). He explained it by saying: either the connection is treated like a pause, or one pauses and begins with ﴿They question one another﴾ ﴿about the great news﴾, with ﴿they question one another﴾ understood as implied, because what follows explains it.

Al-Qurṭubī said: The phrase ﴿about the great news﴾ is not dependent on the ﴿they question one another﴾ mentioned in the recitation. Rather, another verb is understood: ﴿About what do they question one another?﴾ ﴿About the great news﴾. Otherwise the interrogation would have to be repeated: "About the great news?"

In any case, what they questioned one another about was first left vague, then clarified afterward as ﴿the great news﴾. But the explanation of what this great news is remains open. It was said: it is the Messenger (ﷺ) in his mission to them. It was said: it is the Qur'an which was revealed to him, with which he calls them. It was said: it is the resurrection after death.

Ibn Jarīr preferred that all these meanings are intended and that they do not contradict one another.

In reality, they are all interrelated, because whoever denies one of them denies all of them, and whoever affirms one of them affirms all of them, and whoever disagrees about one of them undoubtedly disagrees about all of them.

However, the context concerns "the news," which is singular, so which one is specifically meant here?

Ibn Kathīr and al-Qurṭubī said: whoever said it is the Qur'an bases this on His saying: ﴿Say: It is a great news,﴾ ﴿from which you turn away.﴾ (Ṣād 38:67–68)

Whoever said it is the resurrection bases this on what follows: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgment is an appointed time.﴾ (An-Naba' 78:17)

What appears to me, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that the most evident of these in proof is the Day of Judgment and resurrection, because after it comes the full set of proofs and demonstrations of resurrection, and it is followed by an explicit mention of the Day of Judgment. The proofs of resurrection are known to be four: the creation of the earth and the heavens, the reviving of the earth through plants, the bringing of humans into existence from nothing, and the actual reviving of the dead in this world as a witness to it. All of them are present here.

As for the creation of the earth and the heavens, He alerted to it by His saying: ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting place?﴾ ﴿And the mountains as pegs?﴾ (An-Naba' 78:6–7), and His saying: ﴿And We built above you seven strong ones,﴾ ﴿and We placed a blazing lamp.﴾ (An-Naba' 78:12–13). All of these are cosmic signs indicating His power, as He said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind.﴾ (Ghāfir 40:57)

As for the reviving of the earth through plants, it is in His saying: ﴿And We send down from the rain-clouds abundant water,﴾ ﴿that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation,﴾ ﴿and gardens of dense foliage.﴾ (An-Naba' 78:14–16) As He said: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revived it is the reviver of the dead.﴾ (Fuṣṣilat 41:39)

As for bringing humans into existence from nothing, it is in His saying: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾ (An-Naba' 78:8), meaning kinds. As He said: ﴿Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation.﴾ (Yā-Sīn 36:79)

As for the actual reviving of the dead in this world, it is in His saying: ﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾ (An-Naba' 78:9). [p. 408] Subāt means cessation from movement. It was also said that it is death, a lesser death. Allah called it a taking (tawaffī) in His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those who have not died during their sleep.﴾ (Al-Zumar 39:42) And His saying: ﴿It is He who takes you at night and knows what you have earned by day; then He resurrects you therein.﴾ (Al-Anʿām 6:60) This is like the slain man of the Children of Israel and the birds of Abraham. These are signs of resurrection, all of them mentioned in summary.

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) had already presented them in detail in more than one place. For this reason, Allah followed them with His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgment is an appointed time﴾ (An-Naba' 78:17), meaning for the resurrection about which they disagree. The context thus favors this meaning for "the news" here.

This is further confirmed by the fact that they denied the resurrection far more, and disagreed about it far more intensely, than they did about the prophethood and the Qur'an. Most of them acknowledged the eloquence of the Qur'an and that it is neither magic nor poetry, and they all acknowledged his truthfulness and trustworthiness (peace be upon him). But the intensity of their disagreement about the resurrection appears in the opening of Surah Ṣād and Surah Qāf. In Ṣād, He said: ﴿And they wondered that a warner from among themselves had come to them, and the disbelievers said, "This is a lying sorcerer."﴾ ﴿"Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!"﴾ (Ṣād 38:4–5)

In Qāf, He said: ﴿Rather, they wonder that a warner from among themselves has come to them, and the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing."﴾ ﴿"When we die and become dust, that is a far-off return."﴾ (Qāf 50:2–3) Thus they were more extreme in deeming the resurrection far-fetched than what preceded it. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, they will come to know; then again, nay, they will come to know﴾

He does not specify here whether they (already) knew or not. But the mention of the signs of His manifest power over their being brought back to life after death serves as an informing them of what they differed about, since it is like one who says to them: "If you differ over the affirmation of the Resurrection and its negation, then these are His signs and His proofs; so take heed from them and measure it against them, for the One who is able to bring about those is able to bring about their like."

However, true knowledge through direct witnessing has not yet come, because of the presence of the sin (sa-), which is for the future. It has also come in the surah "At-Takathur" in His saying: ﴿Your competition for more distracts you﴾ ﴿until you visit the graves﴾ ﴿Nay, you will come to know﴾ ﴿then again, nay, you will come to know﴾ ﴿Nay, if you knew with the certainty of knowledge﴾ ﴿you would surely see the Hellfire﴾ ﴿then you will surely see it with the certainty of sight﴾ [At-Takathur: 1-7]. And this which they will come to know is the Day of Decision explicitly mentioned in the context: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time﴾ [An-Naba': 17].

The words of the Most High: ﴿Did We not make the earth a resting-place?﴾

It was recited as "mahdan" in the singular (مَهْدًا), meaning like a cradle (المَهْد) for a child. The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, had already explained this when discussing the words of the Most High: ﴿He who made the earth a resting-place for you and made for you therein roads﴾.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 9:

Allah's saying: ﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾ ﴿And We made the night a covering﴾ ﴿And We made the day a means of livelihood﴾

The explanation of these three (matters) has already been given by the Shaykh, may the mercy of Allah the Exalted be upon us and upon him. (It concerned) the sleep being a subat (a rest, a cessation of activity): either rest or death; and the night being a libas (a garment, a covering): a cover and a source of comfort; and the day being a ma'ash (a means of livelihood): for seeking one's sustenance. That was in his commentary on the saying of Allah the Exalted in surah "al-Furqan": ﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a covering, and sleep as a rest, and made the day a resurrection﴾ [al-Furqan: 47]. All of these are signs indicating the power to resurrect, as the reference to it has already passed.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We built above you seven strong [heavens]﴾

That is: the seven heavens. The explanation of this was already given by the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on us and on him) at His saying, exalted is He, in Surah Qaf: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no fissures?﴾ [Qaf: 6], and he cited similar texts there.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in multitudes.﴾

The blowing of the Trumpet (al-nafkh fi al-sur) is for the Resurrection (al-ba'th), and this is well known. As for "and you will come forth in multitudes" (ta'tunna afwajan): He has already explained the manner of this coming, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will come out of the graves swiftly﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 43], and His saying: ﴿As if they were scattered locusts, hastening toward the caller﴾ [al-Qamar: 7-8]. As for "afwaj" (multitudes, groups) here, it has been said that it means the various nations, as in His saying: ﴿The Day We shall summon every people with their leader, and whoever is given his record in his right hand...﴾ [al-Isra': 71], up to the end of the verse. However, the verse uses the second-person address, "ta'tunna" (you will come), which indicates that the multitudes are of this Ummah.

Al-Qurtubi and others have related a report from Mu'adh, that he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and he said: "O Mu'adh, you have asked about a great matter among matters." Then he let his eyes flow and said: "Ten categories of my Ummah will be gathered," and he related it. Al-Zamakhshari also related it in the same way. Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf: al-Tha'labi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Muhammad ibn Zuhayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hindi, from Hanzalah al-Sadusi, from his father, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, from him (ﷺ), in full, and it is: "Some of them will be in the form of monkeys, some of them in the form of pigs, some of them will be upside down, their feet above their faces, being dragged upon them; some of them will be blind, some deaf and mute, and some of them will be chewing their tongues, which will hang upon their chests, with pus flowing from their mouths, which the people of the gathering will find repulsive; some of them will have their hands and feet cut off; some of them will be crucified on trunks of fire; some of them will be more foul-smelling than carrion; and some of them will be clothed in a garment of tar, sticking to their skins."

As for those in the form of pigs: they are the people of illicit gain (ahl al-suht). The upside-down ones: the consumers of usury (akalat al-riba). The blind: those who are unjust in judgment. The deaf: those who are self-admiring in their deeds. Those who chew their tongues: the scholars and storytellers whose words contradicted their deeds. Those with severed hands and feet: those who harm their neighbours. The crucified: those who inform on people to the authorities. Those who are more foul-smelling: those who follow their desires, and those who withhold the right of Allah from their wealth. Those clothed in the garment: the proud and boastful. The end of the quotation, abridged in wording. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the mountains will be set in motion, and they will become a mirage﴾

The explanation of their condition on the Day of Resurrection has already passed, and the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) had already explained this in detail at His saying, exalted is He, in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿They ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105], and at His saying, exalted is He, in Surah an-Naml: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them solid, while they pass away as the clouds pass﴾ [an-Naml: 88].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 23:

Allah's saying: ﴿Remaining therein for ages﴾ ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink﴾ ﴿except scalding water and dark, foul liquid﴾

He has not specified here how many ages (ahqab) there are, and this is the matter of the fading of the Fire and its non-fading.

It has been said: the meaning of "ahqab" here is a portion of time, not all of it, and these are the ahqab described as their state therein, in what follows from their condition that they will not taste therein, that is, in the Fire, for ages of time, any coolness or drink, except scalding water and dark, foul liquid.

As for the rest of the ahqab, it will be said to them: ﴿So We shall increase you only in punishment﴾ [An-Naba': 30]. This matter has been examined by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, in the book Daf' Iham al-Idtirab (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction), in discussing this verse (p. 411), and in Surah al-An'am on His saying: ﴿The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide eternally, except as Allah wills﴾ [Al-An'am: 128], and it is a lengthy discussion. The book will be published, Allah willing, together with this supplement.

Al-Qurtubi mentioned, regarding the meaning of "huqb" (age), numerous reports, among them: from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "By Allah, whoever enters the Fire will not leave it until he has remained therein for ahqab. A huqb is about eighty-odd years, and a year is three hundred and sixty days, each day is a thousand years of what you count. So let none of you rely on the hope that he will come out of the Fire." Related by al-Tha'labi.

Al-Qurtubi has preferred that their stay—that is, the disbelievers' in the Fire—is forever, for ever and ever. End.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p. 430) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah an-Naba'

His saying: ﴿Remaining therein for ages﴾.

The manner of reconciling this, together with similar verses such as His saying: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾ [Hud: 107], with the verses that necessitate the perpetual continuation of the punishment of the people of the Fire without cessation, such as His saying: ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ [An-Nisa': 57], has already been given in Surah al-An'am in discussing His saying: ﴿The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide eternally, except as Allah wills﴾ [Al-An'am: 128]. There we explained that the punishment does not cease from them, and we explained the manner of the exception by the will of Allah. As for the manner of reconciling the ahqab mentioned here with the eternal perpetuity to which the verses we have cited point, it is in three ways:

The first, which Ibn Jarir inclined to, and which in my view is the most apparent because of the indication of the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, is that His saying: ﴿Remaining therein for ages﴾ is connected to what follows it, i.e., ﴿Remaining therein for ages﴾ in the state in which ﴿they will not taste therein any coolness or drink﴾ ﴿except scalding water and dark, foul liquid﴾ [An-Naba': 23–25]. Then, when those ages have passed, they will be punished with other kinds of punishment besides the scalding water and the dark liquid. What indicates this is His explicit statement that they will be punished with other kinds of punishment besides the scalding water and the dark liquid, in His saying: ﴿This—let them taste it: scalding water and dark liquid, and other punishments of its kind in pairs﴾ [Sad: 57–58].

The most that follows from this view is an overlap of circumstances (tadakhul al-hal), and this is permissible even according to those who prohibit the succession of circumstances (taradduf al-hal), such as Ibn 'Asfur and those who agree with him. Its clarification is that the clause ﴿they will not taste﴾ is a circumstance (hal) of the implicit subject of the active participle, by which we mean His saying "remaining" (labithin), which is itself a circumstance. A parallel to the occurrence in the Qur'an of a negated present-tense verbal clause functioning as a circumstance with "la" is His saying: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing﴾ [An-Nahl: 78], i.e., in the state in which you do not know anything.

The second: that these ahqab never end. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir from Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and he said it is more correct than making the verse refer to the sinning Muslims, as Khalid ibn Ma'dan held.

The third: even if we grant that His saying "ahqaban" indicates finitude and termination, that is understood only from the implication of the adverbial phrase, whereas eternity is explicitly stated in the direct text, and the explicit text takes precedence over the implication, as is established in the principles of jurisprudence. And the view of Khalid ibn Ma'dan that this verse refers to the sinning Muslims is refuted by the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, for Allah said: ﴿And they denied Our signs with complete denial﴾ [An-Naba': 28], and these are the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 29:

﴿And everything We have enumerated in a Book.﴾

It has been said that what is meant by "thing" here is the deeds of the servants, meaning: after His saying ﴿a recompense in accordance [with their deeds]﴾ [An-Naba': 26], that is, in conformity with their deeds without any increase or decrease. He said: "We have enumerated their deeds and recorded them." This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 49].

And His saying: ﴿Not a word does he utter except that with him is an observer, ready [to record]﴾ [Qaf: 18].

And His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 7-8].

And His saying: ﴿Allah has enumerated it, though they have forgotten it﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 6].

The wording is general for everything, and what supports this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, all things We created with predestination﴾ [Al-Qamar: 49]. "Predestination" (qadar) carries the meaning of enumeration. In the Sunnah there is the well-known hadith of the pen. And [there is] His saying: ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register﴾ [Ya-Sin: 12]. And His saying, exalted is He, has already passed in Surah "al-Jinn": ﴿And He has encompassed what is with them and has enumerated everything in number﴾ [Al-Jinn: 28].

This verse is among the greatest proofs of His power, the breadth of His knowledge, and that nothing ever escapes Him, and that He knows the particulars just as He knows the universals.

As has passed in Surah "al-Mujadilah": ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth, nor fewer than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 7].

(p-412) Likewise is the detail in His saying: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain within the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but that it is in a clear register﴾.

Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing is a triumph (mafaz)﴾

He clarified it afterwards by His saying: ﴿gardens and grapevines﴾, up to His saying: ﴿a recompense from your Lord, a gift reckoned (as sufficient)﴾ [An-Naba': 32–36].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As a reward from your Lord, a gift reckoned in full﴾ (ʿaṭāʾan ḥisāban).

Regarding the disbelievers He said: ﴿a fitting recompense﴾ (jazāʾan wifāqan), and regarding the believers He said ﴿a gift reckoned in full﴾ (ʿaṭāʾan ḥisāban).

In the first, there is a statement that their recompense corresponds to their deeds, and ﴿your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾. In the second, there is a statement that this bliss is a gift from Allah and a bounty bestowed upon them from the very beginning, and it is the triumph (al-mafāz) explained in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to the Garden has indeed triumphed﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 185].

Entry into the Garden at the outset is a gift from Allah, as in the hadith: "None of you will enter the Garden by his deeds" (lan yadkhula aḥadukum al-jannata bi-ʿamalihi). And His saying ﴿reckoned﴾ (ḥisāban) indicates that the differences in rank among the people of the Garden within the Garden are according to reckoning and the outcomes of deeds. It has also been said that ﴿ḥisāban﴾ means "sufficiency" (kifāyah), so that each one of them says: "ḥasbī, ḥasbī" (sufficient for me, sufficient for me), i.e., "kāfīnī" (suffice me).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 38:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿The Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows﴾. The explanation of this was already given by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, when speaking on the words of Allah the Exalted in Surah "al-Kahf": ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows﴾ [al-Kahf: 48].

Ibn Kathir mentioned seven opinions concerning the meaning of "the Spirit" here: the spirits of the children of Adam; or the children of Adam themselves; or a creation of Allah's creation in the forms of the children of Adam, who are neither angels nor humans, and who eat and drink (p-413); or Jibril; or the Qur'an; or a great angel equal in size to all of creation. Al-Zamakhshari related them, and al-Qurtubi reported them and added an eighth: that they are guardians over the angels. Ibn Jarir hesitated to give preference to any one of them.

What the Qur'an supports with a text similar to this one is that it refers to Jibril, peace be upon him, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by the permission of their Lord with every matter﴾ [al-Qadr: 4]. In it, the angels are mentioned after the Spirit by way of mentioning the general after the specific, while in Surah "al-Qadr" the specific is mentioned after the general. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿None will speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Because of the severity of the terror of the standing-place. And these, who are the most honoured of creation before Allah and the closest to Allah, will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted; so others among creation are more so by way of greater reason.

Ibn Kathir said: It is like the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission﴾ [Hud: 105], and like the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

The reality is that all of this indicates that on that Day there is no authority or dominion for anyone, not even a word, except what has been permitted in it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 39:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿That is the true Day﴾

It is the Day of Resurrection. The demonstrative is "that" (dhalika), and it has been indicated with the demonstrative particle specific to the distant, "dhalika" instead of "hadha" (this), even though the speech concerns something near. This is either because it is distant in time from the time of speaking about it, or because of the loftiness of its rank and the greatness of its matter, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim﴾ ﴿That is the Book﴾ [al-Baqarah: 1-2]. In this there is a return to a beginning at the start of the surah, namely that when they were asking in astonishment or denying the Day of Resurrection, they would come to know its truth, and here it is, the true Day, with no doubt or uncertainty in it, and they will see it with the certainty of sight ('ayn al-yaqin).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then whoever wills takes to his Lord a return (ma'ab)﴾.

Ma'ab means the place of return, as has been mentioned previously in a similar form: ﴿Whoever wills takes to his Lord a way﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 19]. So when this Day is a certain truth, and people in it are either headed to Hell, ﴿It has been a lying-in-wait﴾ ﴿a place of return for the tyrants﴾ [al-Naba': 21-22], or to a ﴿place of success﴾ ﴿gardens and vineyards﴾ [al-Naba': 31-32], then after this explanation: ﴿Whoever wills takes to his Lord a return﴾, he returns to his Lord to a return that he desires for himself. And "whoever wills" here is explicit in giving choice, but the context is not a context of choice; rather it is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve. Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire﴾, and so on [al-Kahf: 29].

So it is closer to a threat, just as it also takes into account the will of the servant in what he pursues. And Allah, may He be exalted, knows best.

And what comes after it indicates the threat.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 78, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾

And His saying: ﴿The Day when a man will look upon what his hands have sent forth﴾ [An-Naba': 40]. All of this is a severe warning and a strong exhortation to earnestly strive to do good and to seek salvation on the true Day. We ask Allah for safety and well-being.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Day when a man will look upon what his hands have sent forth﴾

Allah, exalted is He, has explained the outcome of this looking: either joy at it or terror from it, as in His saying: ﴿The Day when every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that were a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the [His] servants﴾ [Al 'Imran: 30].
